The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!
The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!
3E.3 We should pray to be delivered from lying lips that speak contemptuously against the righteous.
12E.9 Slander is a characteristic of the wicked.
22F.9 Pray to God for deliverance from enemies, and that they may not triumph over you.

precepts.text: For I have heard the slander of many: while they took counsel together against me, they devised to take away my life. Slander is not a light thing.
precepts.point: But when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon's faction murders were committed: Simon hated Onias so much he had one of his men kill one of Onias's priests. That is why I say it is never just one thing; it is a domino effect of sins.
precepts.why:
Simon slandered Onias the third. So how serious is slander? “For I have heard the slander of many: fear was on every side: while they took counsel together against me, they devised to take away my life.”

Slander is not a light thing. It is the first step of a counsel against a man’s life. The ones who slander take counsel together, and what they devise is to take away his life.

That is exactly the road Simon walked. He slandered Onias to the Greeks, and it did not stop at words: “when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon’s faction murders were committed”. The slander of many leads to the taking of life.

precepts.text: Righteousness is observing to do all these commandments before the Most High as He commanded us.
precepts.point: If we are doing the righteousness of the Most High, which is keeping His commandments, we will not be put to shame, and that is why David prays this thing.

note.label: Psalm 31: In Thee O Lord Do I Put My Trust

precepts.why:
David prays “deliver me in thy righteousness”, and asks “let me never be ashamed”. Moses shows what the righteousness of the Most High is: “it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.” Righteousness is keeping his commandments.

This is a psalm of David dealing with his commitment to the Most High. If we are doing the righteousness of the Most High, which is keeping his commandments, we will not be put to shame, and that is why David prays this thing.

moments.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: Oh how great is thy goodness, which thou hast laid up for them that fear thee. Keep the fear of God on you, because in the end you get God's goodness. Trust in God, not in the people that are big, bad, and prideful; their time is temporary.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: Thou shalt hide them in the secret of thy presence from the pride of man. What we know is a secret: we are learning we are the Israelites of a Bible they took away from us and told us this is not your book. Thou shalt keep them secretly in a pavilion from the strife of tongues: they speak evil against us, but God keeps us in a secret place from it.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: In thee O Lord do I put my trust, let me never be ashamed, deliver me in thy righteousness. This is a psalm of David dealing with his commitment to the Most High.
If we are doing the righteousness of the Most High, which is keeping His commandments, we will not be put to shame, and that is why David prays this thing.

note.label: Psalm 31: In Thee O Lord Do I Put My Trust

points: Bow down thine ear to me, deliver me speedily, be thou my strong rock and a house of defense to save me, for thou art my rock and my fortress. For thy name's sake lead me and guide me, and pull me out of the net that they have laid privily for me, for thou art my strength.

note.label: Psalm 31: In Thee O Lord Do I Put My Trust

points: Into thine hand I commit my spirit, thou hast redeemed me O Lord God of truth. I have hated them that regard lying vanities, but I trust in the Lord and will be glad and rejoice in thy mercy, for thou hast considered my trouble and known my soul in adversities.

note.label: Psalm 31: In Thee O Lord Do I Put My Trust

points: Thou hast not shut me up into the hand of the enemy but hast set my feet in a large room. The reading stresses that David has hated them that regard lying vanities while still trusting in the Lord.

note.label: Psalm 31: In Thee O Lord Do I Put My Trust

points: Have mercy upon me O Lord for I am in trouble, my eye is consumed with grief, my soul and my belly, for my life is spent with grief and my years with sighing, my strength faileth because of my iniquity and my bones are consumed.

note.label: Psalm 31: In Thee O Lord Do I Put My Trust

points: I was a reproach among all my enemies but especially among my neighbors and a fear to mine acquaintance, they that did see me without fled from me, I am forgotten as a dead man out of mind, I am like a broken vessel. Fear was on every side while they took counsel together against me and devised to take away my life.

note.label: Psalm 31: In Thee O Lord Do I Put My Trust

points: But I trusted in thee O Lord, I said thou art my God, my times are in thy hand, deliver me from the hand of mine enemies and from them that persecute me. Make thy face to shine upon thy servant and save me for thy mercy's sake. Let the wicked be ashamed and silent in the grave, and let the lying lips be put to silence.

note.label: Psalm 31: In Thee O Lord Do I Put My Trust

points: Oh how great is thy goodness which thou hast laid up for them that fear thee and wrought for them that trust in thee before the sons of men. Thou shalt hide them in the secret of thy presence from the pride of man and keep them secretly in a pavilion from the strife of tongues.

note.label: Psalm 31: In Thee O Lord Do I Put My Trust

points: Blessed be the Lord for He hath showed me His marvelous kindness in a strong city, and though David said in his haste he was cut off, the Lord heard the voice of his supplications when he cried unto Him. Love the Lord all ye His saints, for the Lord preserveth the faithful and plentifully rewardeth the proud doer.

note.label: Psalm 31: In Thee O Lord Do I Put My Trust

points: Be of good courage and He shall strengthen your heart, all ye that hope in the Lord. David has committed himself to the Most High and is asking for specific things against his enemies. This is a prayer for protection and vengeance, which is what we need to be doing in these last days, embedding ourselves into the prayers of our forefathers. If you do not know what to say in your prayer, turn to the book of Psalms and use these prayers in your daily life to invoke the spirit of the Most High in this earth that He will come and redeem us out of this captivity.
